steps: Check code & permits
Install to CAN/CSA-B365 and local code; consult local building officials on restrictions and inspection first. Never install in any fireplace or connect to an air distribution duct or system.

Install to CAN/CSA-B365 and local code. Local building officials have the final authority to approve the installation; discuss it with them before you begin.

The data plate on the back of the stove gives the safety testing information, the certified testing laboratory and the installation requirements.

Never install in any fireplace, and never connect to any air distribution duct or system.
Unpack & fit baffles

Check the fire bricks haven't shifted and the air control works freely. Fit legs, handle and baffles per the separate Assembly Instructions: two cast iron baffles above the three stainless secondary-air pipes, carbowool blanket on top.

After unpacking, check that the fire bricks are firmly in position and the air control works freely. Legs, handle fitting and baffles follow the separate Assembly Instructions.

The baffles ship inside the stove. Place the two cast iron baffles above the three stainless pipes that supply the secondary air, then lay the carbowool blanket carefully on top. Before the first fire, confirm the upper heating shield, baffles and blanket are placed correctly.

Standard accessories (a Morsø glove and a ceramic flue connection gasket) are usually in the ashpan or firebox.
Plan the chimney
Dedicated flue, not less than 6 inches: code-approved masonry with flue liner or listed type HT (UL-103-1985). Independently supported, not on the stove; at least 16 feet above the stove recommended.
Set the flue outlet

Ships with the collar on the top plate and a blanking plate on the rear exit. For rear: knock out the round panel in the rear heat shield, untwist and swap the blanking plate and collar, push down and tighten the screws.
Connect the chimney connector

6 inches; 24 gauge or heavier single wall (no galvanized) or listed double wall, three screws per joint. Horizontal run max 3 feet, total 8 feet, no more than two 90 degree turns, rising 1/4 inch per foot.
Position to clearances
Hold the standard or alcove clearances (minimum tested distances). At least 4 inches is recommended to non-combustible materials; increase distances for heat-sensitive materials.
Lay floor protection
Non-combustible, beneath the heater: US 16" to the front and 6" to the sides of the loading door and ash openings; Canada 450 mm (18 in) on door sides, 200 mm (8 in) on others.
Mobile home (US only)
Outside combustion air kit, spark-arrestor cap, listed Type HT connector and chimney (never single wall); bolt the stove through the hearth pad into the flooring. Per 24 CFR, Part 3280 (HUD).
Combustion air

If room leakage isn't sufficient, add a dedicated inlet with 2 square inches (1250 square mm) free air space. Never draw combustion air from a wall, floor or ceiling cavity, attic or garage. Do not install in a sleeping room.

A dedicated fresh air inlet matters most in a well-sealed room, or where an extractor hood or ventilation system disturbs the natural air pressure. Don't put it on a wall usually under negative pressure from normal wind, or directly across the room from the stove (cold draft).

Never draw combustion air from a wall, floor or ceiling cavity or from any enclosed space such as an attic or garage. Do not install in a sleeping room.

Keep furniture at least 30 inches from the stove.
First fire
Confirm the baffles and blanket are in place. Keep the first fire small so the paint cures and the main plates settle; ventilate the room for the paint fumes.

panels.title: Smoke on lighting or reloading
items: Poor chimney draft (almost certainly the cause)
Insufficient fresh air getting into the room (a very few cases)
Door opened too fast: open 1-2" first, let the flue pressure equalise
Door opened while the stove is being fired vigorously

panels.title: Sluggish or hard to control
items: Soot fall around the flue collar or in the flue/chimney
Flue significantly larger than 6 inches: flue gases cool excessively
Overly dry, gray wood: back-puffing and sluggishness
Hardened door gasket letting air leak in

panels.title: Dirty glass
items: Logs too large or not split
Combustion temperatures too low, or stove run too slowly

panels.title: Over-firing & fast wear
items: Any part of the stove or connector glows: over-firing
Persistent heavy firing; soot and ashes left to accumulate
Ash built up under the grate traps heat: premature grate failure

light.title: Lighting a fire
light.html:
Morsø recommends the "top-down" method and calls it the most environmentally friendly way to light. A cold stove needs plenty of air at first.

  1. Lay a 5-6 inch layer of dry kindling sticks, about 2-4 lbs. Put two firelighters directly under the top layer of sticks. This keeps soot on the glass to a minimum.
  2. Open the primary air completely: move the lever over the door to the right.
  3. Light the fire.
  4. Once the firelighters catch, leave the door ajar about 1" so the chimney draws well. Stay with the stove while the door is open.
  5. After 5-10 minutes the draft should be going. Close the door. A good layer of embers starts to build after another 15 - 20 minutes.
Note: step 2 on p. 13 says to fully open the secondary air supply "controlled by lever beneath the ash lip," but p. 12 says the primary air lever is over the door and the secondary air is fixed open and not adjustable.

Your very first fire

Keep it small, so the paint can cure and the stove's plates can settle into position. The paint gives off some fumes, so ventilate the room.

Never use chemicals or fluids to start a fire, and never burn flammable fluids. Never use gasoline, gasoline-type lantern fuel, kerosene, charcoal lighter or fluid, or similar liquids to start or freshen up a fire. Keep all such liquids away from the stove while it is in use. Don't use a grate, andirons or anything else to raise the fire. Keep the ash door closed while the stove is burning.

air.title: Using the air control
air.html:
The lever over the door controls the primary air. Move it to the right to open it and to the left to close it. This air is preheated and comes in through the "airwash" system above the glass.

Openlever to the right
Medium burn1/4 inch from closed
Minimum burnlever completely to the left (closed)

The secondary air is fed into the gases above the fire for a cleaner, more efficient burn. It is fixed open and can't be adjusted.

Turning it down

  • A few minutes after new wood catches, set the air to suit the heat you want.
  • Always leave enough air for clear, lasting flames. Clear, yellow flames mean the air is adequate.
  • Before you go to the minimum setting, burn at medium for about 15 minutes so the fire is well established.
  • Less heat: less wood, less air. More heat: more wood, more air. Keep a good layer of embers either way.
Note: p. 12 says the secondary air is fixed open and not adjustable, but lighting step 2 on p. 13 says to fully open "the secondary air supply that is controlled by lever beneath the ash lip."
Don't try to get more heat by changing the air control's range. The minimum burn rate is set at the factory, and federal rules forbid altering it.

reload.title: Reloading the stove
reload.html:
Add wood while there's still a good bed of glowing embers. Wood that doesn't catch can, in an extreme case, make the flue gases ignite.

  1. Open the door gently, just 1-2" at first. Wait a few seconds for the pressure in the flue to even out, then open it all the way. This stops smoke spilling out, especially when the draft is poor.
  2. Spread the embers across the bottom, with most toward the front.
  3. Lay two pieces of wood, roughly 2-4 pound and about 10" long, across the embers in one layer, about 1/2" apart.
  4. Close the door with the primary air fully open. The new wood should catch in a few minutes.
  5. After a few minutes, turn the air down to suit the heat you want.
Recommended load4 lbs (2 pieces) up to 6 lbs (4-6 pieces)
Note: the manual gives a maximum recommended load of 6 lbs on pp. 12, 14, 15 and 16, but its safety summary on p. 28 says to refuel with 2-5 pieces, no more than 10 lbs.

Never overload the firebox. Keep the wood below the lowest secondary air tube and the top edge of the back wall's stone lining. The space above is reserved for burning off the gases.

Don't open the door while the fire is burning hard. If smoke comes out when you light or reload, a poor chimney draft is almost certainly to blame. Ask your stove supplier how to improve it.

wood.title: Choosing and seasoning wood
wood.html:
Your stove is listed for wood only. Any natural wood works, as long as it is well seasoned and dry.

Lengthmax 12 inches (30 cm)
Maker's website: Log Size 16.5".
Thicknessapprox. 3 to 3.5 inches (7-8 cm)
Weight per piecearound 2 lbs
Moistureno more than 20%

Split each log down the middle so moisture can escape. A moisture meter makes checking easy; Morsø sells one (part # 62929900).

Seasoning

Stack wood under cover in an airy spot where air moves around each piece. Some soft woods dry in one good summer; oak, maple and elm can take up to 18 months. Seasoned wood feels light and shows cracks running out from the center at the ends. If it spits or sizzles and the glass keeps misting up, it isn't seasoned. Very dry, gray wood can also make smoke puff back and the fire turn sluggish.

Never burn

Garbage, lawn clippings or yard waste, materials containing rubber (including tires), materials containing plastic, waste petroleum products, paints or paint thinners, asphalt products, materials containing asbestos, construction or demolition debris, railroad ties or pressure-treated wood, manure or animal remains, salt-water driftwood or other materials previously saturated with salt water, unseasoned wood, or paper products, cardboard, plywood and particleboard. Burning these materials may release toxic fumes, or make the stove ineffective and cause smoke. Fire starters made from paper, cardboard, sawdust, wax and similar substances are fine for starting a fire.

Note: the manual gives the log thickness as approx. 3 to 3.5 inches (7-8 cm) on p. 11 and as 3-5" thick in its safety summary on p. 28.

safety.title: Safety and over-firing
safety.html:
• The stove is hot while it's burning. Keep children, clothing and furniture away; touching it can burn skin.
  • Keep furniture at least 30 inches away, and the same for things like drying clothes, newspapers and firewood.
  • Burn only with the door fully closed. Never leave the stove alone with the door open: smoke and flame can be drawn out.
  • The manual's safety summary says never burn overnight.
  • Fit a smoke detector in the stove room, but not right next to the stove, where a puff of smoke while reloading can set it off. Put at least one on each floor, close to sleeping areas. Some areas also require carbon monoxide detectors.

Signs of over-firing

Do not over-fire the stove. If any part of the stove or the chimney connector glows, you are over-firing. That can cause a house fire or permanently damage the stove.

Normal flue temperatureapprox. 300° C (550°F)
Must not exceed450° C (750°F)

Those are stove-pipe readings about 20 cm (8") above the stove. A Morsø Flue Gas Thermometer (part # 62901200) attaches with a magnet and shows them.

glass.title: Cleaning the glass
glass.html:
Run the stove at the right temperature and the glass should stay mostly clean. Soot that settles while you light usually burns off as the stove heats up.

  1. Wait until the glass is cold. Never clean it hot.
  2. For heavier deposits that won't burn off, use Morsø glass cleaner, following its instructions.
  3. Never use abrasive cleaners on the glass.

Why it gets dirty

  • Wood that's too wet
  • Logs too large or not split
  • A fire burning too cool, or a stove run too slowly
Cracked or broken glass? Don't use the stove until it's replaced. Use only the high-temperature ceramic glass Morsø supplies; ask your Morsø dealer.

To avoid breaking it, don't strike the glass or slam the door. Old ceramic glass can't be recycled with ordinary glass. Hand it in at a recycling station as ceramic glass.

ash.title: Emptying the ash
ash.html:
Empty the ash pan every day, or as needed. Ash that builds up toward the underside of the grate traps heat and can make the grate fail early. Never empty the stove while it's in operation.

  1. Open the front door. Use a shovel or poker to stir extra ash through the slots in the grate into the ash pan.
  2. Open the ash door and take out the ash pan. Keep it level so no ash spills.
  3. Empty it into a metal container with a tight-fitting lid.
  4. Put the ash pan back and close the ash door.

Set the closed container on a noncombustible floor or on the ground, well away from anything that can burn. If you'll bury or spread the ash, keep it in the closed container until all the cinders are thoroughly cool.

Leave a little ash in the firebox. Always keep a 1-1.5 inch (2-3 cm) layer of ash on the firebox floor. Never use a household or shop vacuum to remove ash.

chimney.title: Chimney, creosote and chimney fires
chimney.html:
Burning wood slowly makes tar and vapors that condense in a cool chimney as creosote. If creosote ignites, it makes an extremely hot fire.

  • Inspect the chimney and the chimney connector (the pipe from the stove to the chimney) at least once every two months during the heating season. Remove any creosote buildup.
  • At first, check for soot above the baffle plate and around the flue outlet every month or so.
  • If the stove suddenly turns sluggish, check for fallen soot around the flue collar or in the chimney.
  • Clean the chimney after each heating season, and inspect it before the next one for bird's nests or other blockages.

To inspect it yourself, let the stove cool completely, then use a mirror to look up through the flue collar into the chimney. If you can't inspect or clean it yourself, contact your Morsø dealer or a professional chimney sweep.

If you have a chimney fire, act promptly: 1. Close the air control. 2. Get everyone out of the house. 3. Call the fire department.

care.title: Yearly care and summer storage
care.html:
Before each heating season

  • Thoroughly clean the chimney and chimney connector, and check them for damage.
  • Check the door gasket for wear or compression; replace it if needed.
  • Check the glass for cracks, and the door and handles for tightness.
  • Lubricate the hinges and closing mechanism once a year or as needed, with copper grease or another heat-resistant grease.

The door gasket hardens over time. Replace it if the door gets hard to close, or if air leaks in around it and the fire gets harder to control. Your stove supplier has a Morsø rope gasket kit.

Over the summer

Clean the stove out thoroughly when the season ends. Ash left in an unused stove soaks up moisture and causes rust. Leave the air control slightly open so air keeps moving through. Keep rainwater out with a chimney cap, but don't block the flue completely. A desiccant such as kitty litter in the ash pan helps; remove it before the heating season.

The outside

Clean the painted surface with a vacuum's soft brush or a lint-free cloth. If it turns slightly gray, Morsø touch-up spray paint is available. It smells a little as it cures on the next fire, so ventilate the room.

warranty.title: Warranty at a glance
warranty.html:
Morsø gives a 10-year limited warranty from the date of purchase, provided the stove was supplied by an authorized Morsø dealer. It covers repair or replacement of parts that are defective in materials or workmanship. The warranty certificate describes it as covering manufacturing defects in the main exterior body parts.

Not covered

  • Installation or use that doesn't follow the manual, local regulations or Morsø's assembly and firing instructions
  • Damage from overheating or burning the wrong fuel
  • Normal wear such as discolored surfaces, and wear parts: smoke deflector plates, grates, refractory stones and plates, glass and sealing materials
  • Repairs or changes Morsø didn't authorize
  • Corrosion after a lack of maintenance or damage to the surface finish
  • Problems caused by local conditions, draft, or the chimney

The warranty is void if the stove isn't installed, operated and maintained as the manual says, if it burns materials it isn't certified for, or if it's modified without authorization.

Making a claim

Contact Morsø Customer Service at info@morsoe.com or +45 96691900. Have your proof of purchase, the model and serial number, and a description of the problem, with photos if possible.

specChimney.title: Chimney
specChimney.html:
Connector & chimney, internalnot less than 6 inches diameter (or equivalent cross section)
USAcode-approved masonry with flue liner, or listed type HT factory-built (UL-103-1985, 2100º F)
CanadaHigh Temperature (650ºC), ULC S-629
Recommended heightat least 16 feet above the stove (not required), flue collar to top

One flueway per appliance; never shared with another appliance. The flue system must be independently secured, not supported by the stove, and a chimney connector is required (don't install the chimney directly at the outlet). Seal every joint so the system is airtight to the chimney outlet (p. 6). Don't oversize: a flue significantly larger than 6 inches lets the gases cool, making the stove sluggish or unpredictable. Roof construction, large trees nearby and high altitude can affect draft and height.

specConn.title: Chimney connector
specConn.html:
Diameter6 inches (150mm)
Single wall24 MSG black or blue; 24 gauge or heavier steel
Double walltested and listed for solid-fuel appliances
Fasteningmin. three screws to the stove and to each section
Horizontal runrecommended max 3 feet (1 metre); slope up 1/4 inch per foot (20 mm per metre)
Total lengthno longer than 8 feet (2.5 metres)
Turnsno more than two 90 degree; prefer mild bends (45º)
Horizontal runs to ceiling18 inches

No galvanized connector: it can't withstand the flue temperatures and may release toxic fumes. Avoid combustible walls and ceilings; a combustible wall pass-through must conform to CAN/CSA-B365. Never through an attic, closet or similar concealed space. Keep all venting accessible for cleaning.

specFloor.title: Floor protection
specFloor.html:
The heater meets CAN/ULC-S627 for installation on a combustible floor without radiant floor protection (p. 8). The protector is for falling embers: non-combustible, extending beneath the heater.

USA · front of loading door & ash opening16"
USA · sides of loading door & ash opening6"
Canada · any side with a doorat least 450 mm (18 in), full width plus 200 mm (8 in) each side
Canada · other sidesat least 200 mm (8 in)

Canada (CSA B365): a continuous, durable, non-combustible ember pad. Where the appliance is less than 200 mm (8 in) from a wall, the pad need only extend to the base of the wall. Not on top of carpet unless structurally supported against displacement and distortion.

specMobile.title: Mobile home installation (US only)
specMobile.html:
The 7110 C can be installed in a US mobile home if it meets all of these:

  • Outside combustion air kit, installed per the kit's guide; intake piping through the floor into a vented crawl space or through the wall.
  • Listed Type HT chimney connector, HT chimney and terminal cap with spark arrestor. Never a single wall connector (stovepipe).
  • Stove secured to the structure by bolting through the hearth pad into the flooring.
  • Floor protection per section 1.5, followed precisely.
  • Top chimney sections removable for a maximum clearance of 13.5' from ground level for transportation.
  • Installed in accordance with 24 CFR, Part 3280 (HUD).

Maintain the structural integrity of the mobile home floor, wall and ceiling/roof: don't cut through floor joists, wall studs or ceiling trusses (p. 10).

Note: p. 9 says "Canada: do not install in a transportable building / mobile home" and that mobile home installation applies to the USA only, yet the same list of mobile home requirements also gives Canadian ones: a 6" (152 mm) factory-built chimney to CAN/ULC-629M, plus a Canadian floor protector.

review.notes: Manual covers the Morsø 7110 C (cover, p. 3, parts list pp. 22-23); the p. 21 exploded drawing is titled 'Morsø 7110 B' (drawing 7100-502, 2019). Title uses the catalog name 7110 B; model_line uses the manual's 7110 C. Catalog model number 64710221, firebox 0.83 cu ft, heating area 1300 sq ft, height/width/depth, weight 309 lb and 'tertiary air' (features) are not in the manual, so not checked. Pages 7, 26 and 27 have no extractable text (figure or blank pages). The p. 9 floor-protection drawing labels (e.g. '0" MIN.' at the backwall) are not transcribed beyond what the p. 9 text states. p. 16 prints 300° C (550°F) and 450° C (750°F); the °C and °F figures don't correspond exactly. Shown as printed. p. 5 says a chimney connector is included with the heater, while p. 6 describes only the factory-fitted flue collar and tells the installer which connector to use; confirm what ships. The p. 10 warnings (no combustion air from cavities/attic/garage, do not install in a sleeping room) follow the mobile-home section without saying they apply only to mobile homes; shown as general warnings. The 'no grate / build fire directly on hearth' warning (pp. 10-11) is kept although the stove has its own grate with ash slots (p. 19); owner text says not to use a grate or andirons to raise the fire. Door-ajar wording differs slightly (p. 13 intro 'an inch or two', step 4 'about 1'''); not flagged. 'kitter litter' (p. 20) written as kitty litter. No blower, burn-time or troubleshooting chart in the manual; fault panels are drawn from the draft (p. 16), dirty-glass (p. 17), gasket and wear (p. 18), flue-size (p. 5) and ash (p. 19) text. No code table.
